gen_risks.description: Low market uptake of the newly introduced Sustainability‑Linked and Green Loans may limit financing reach.
gen_risks.mitigation: Run targeted outreach and pilot incentives; partner with anchor firms to create demand for sustainable loans.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 7: first systematic application of SLLs in Mexico; market for sustainable finance remains nascent and concentrated among large corporations.

gen_risks.description: Participating Financial Institutions lack capacity to design, appraise and monitor green loan portfolios.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide dedicated technical assistance, standardized appraisal tools and training workshops for PFIs.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 15: limited capacity of Mexican financial institutions to design, originate, appraise and monitor green loans.

gen_risks.description: High Monitoring, Reporting and Verification (MRV) costs deter SMEs from applying for sustainable finance.
gen_risks.mitigation: Subsidize MRV expenses, develop a shared verification platform and simplify reporting templates.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 15: high Monitoring, Reporting and Verification (MRV) costs and limited capacity hinder SME loan uptake.

gen_risks.description: Credit risk of beneficiary enterprises could lead to loan defaults and affect project financial viability.
gen_risks.mitigation: Apply rigorous credit assessments, require co‑financing, and use step‑down pricing incentives tied to performance.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 30: NAFIN assumes credit risk of BEs; Section 19 notes extreme temperatures raise loan delinquency rates.

gen_risks.description: Physical climate hazards (heatwaves, floods) may impair SME operations and repayment capacity.
gen_risks.mitigation: Integrate climate‑resilience criteria in loan eligibility and offer insurance or contingency funding for high‑risk firms.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 19: Mexico faces significant climate vulnerability; extreme weather increases operational costs and financial distress for SMEs.

gen_risks.description: Insufficient co‑financing from firms or PFIs could limit the amount of private capital mobilized.
gen_risks.mitigation: Enforce minimum co‑financing thresholds, provide matching grant incentives, and engage private investors early in pipeline development.
gen_risks.evidence: Sections 28‑29: require minimum 20% co‑financing from BEs and 30% from PFIs for sub‑projects.

gen_risks.description: Gender gap in access to finance may reduce participation of women‑led enterprises, undermining inclusive outcomes.
gen_risks.mitigation: Set gender‑inclusive eligibility criteria, allocate a quota for women‑led firms, and run gender‑focused outreach campaigns.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 46: 14% gender gap in finance; women‑owned firms have lower credit access.

gen_risks.description: Risk of greenwashing if sustainability plans are not properly validated, compromising environmental integrity.
gen_risks.mitigation: Mandate independent ex‑ante validation and ex‑post verification for all sustainability plans; conduct random audits.
gen_risks.evidence: Section on SLL validation: ex‑ante validation and ex‑post verification required to mitigate greenwashing risk.

gen_risks.description: Procurement capacity gaps at NAFIN may delay contract award and implementation of TA activities.
gen_risks.mitigation: Appoint a qualified internal procurement professional and provide hands‑on training with World Bank support.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 57‑58: NAFIN staff lack direct procurement experience; internal procurement professional to be appointed.

gen_risks.description: Fiduciary risk from reliance on legacy manual financial systems could cause errors or delays in fund tracking.
gen_risks.mitigation: Upgrade FM systems, automate reconciliations, and conduct periodic internal and external audits.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 54‑55: residual FM risk moderate; efficiency constraints from legacy manual systems.

gen_risks.description: Changes to the Sustainable Taxonomy or ESG standards may affect eligibility of projects and loan terms.
gen_risks.mitigation: Monitor policy developments, keep eligibility criteria flexible, and maintain dialogue with regulators and taxonomy authorities.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 7: Sustainable Taxonomy provides criteria but policy may evolve, affecting eligibility.

gen_risks.description: Shift in government priorities could reduce political support or funding for the project.
gen_risks.mitigation: Secure formal commitments through memoranda of understanding and align project outputs with national development plans.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 2.A.2: Plan México launched 2025; new administration may shift priorities.

gen_risks.description: Anchor companies may not demand sustainable suppliers, limiting the incentive for firms to adopt green practices.
gen_risks.mitigation: Engage anchor firms early, develop supplier‑development programs, and link financing to procurement contracts.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 9‑10: anchor companies expect sustainable suppliers; many SMEs not prepared.

gen_risks.description: Complex coordination among NAFIN, PFIs and the World Bank could cause implementation delays.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish clear governance structures, regular coordination meetings, and documented decision‑making protocols.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 38‑39: Project Implementation Team coordinates NAFIN, PFIs, WB; coordination risks noted.

gen_risks.description: Substantial environmental and social risk classification may trigger compliance challenges and project delays.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement a robust ESMS, conduct thorough due diligence, and monitor compliance with regular reporting.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 60: Environmental and Social risk classified as Substantial.

gen_risks.description: Currency fluctuations could affect the real cost of MXN‑denominated loans for borrowers and lenders.
gen_risks.mitigation: Use FX swaps to hedge exposure and limit the share of USD‑denominated loans.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 31: NAFIN will manage FX risk using Mexico’s currency swap market.

gen_risks.description: Failure to mobilize the targeted US$89 million of private capital would reduce overall impact.
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop a pipeline of bankable projects, offer de‑risking instruments, and engage private investors early.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 28: project aims to mobilize US$89 million private capital; shortfall risk.

gen_risks.description: Weak anti‑corruption controls could expose the project to fraud or reputational damage.
gen_risks.mitigation: Strengthen anti‑corruption policies, train staff, and implement a whistle‑blower mechanism with regular audits.
gen_risks.evidence: Loan Agreement sections require compliance with Anti‑Corruption Guidelines and fraud detection provisions.

gt_risks.description: The Project channels financing to SMEs/mid-caps via NAFIN through Green Loans (GLs) and Sustainability-Linked Loans (SLLs). For GLs, E&S risk is limited (resources go to a pre-screened positive list), but SLLs operate as corporate loans, making site-specific impacts harder to trace and creating risk around traceability of environmental outcomes and possible greenwashing if sustainability targets are weak or under-monitored.
gt_risks.mitigation: NAFIN prepared an Environmental and Social Management System (ESMS) summary covering main E&S risks by key sector, disclosed at appraisal.

gt_risks.description: Introduction of new financial instruments (notably SLLs) not currently deployed in Mexico, which may lack sufficient demand, drives the technical design risk rating.
gt_risks.mitigation: Substantial TA to NAFIN, PFIs, and beneficiary enterprises (BEs) to support instrument design/deployment; GFPP grant to advance instrument design during preparation; NAFIN required to prepare and adopt a Sustainable Finance Framework (covering SLLs and GLs) acceptable to the Bank prior to effectiveness; draw on global best practices from comparable SLL facilities; Bank hands-on support during initial deployment.

gt_risks.description: The Project requires close coordination and participation of several stakeholders: different units within NAFIN, participating financial institutions (PFIs), beneficiary enterprises, and large anchor companies heading the green value chains (GVCs).
gt_risks.mitigation: Develop and deploy engagement/communication strategies pre-implementation via GFPP plus ongoing TA; establish a dedicated project implementation team within NAFIN with clear roles/responsibilities; formalize PFI participation through legal agreements defining reporting obligations and performance expectations; proactive NAFIN/WB engagement with anchor companies to encourage supplier-firm participation.

gt_risks.description: Risk that SMEs, mid-caps, and participating financial institutions may not take up the new SLL/GL products at the expected pace or scale, given evolving global sustainability policies, limited familiarity with the instruments, and possible overestimation of market demand.
gt_risks.mitigation: NAFIN business-development efforts for sustainable finance; targeted awareness and capacity-building for potential borrowers; TA to help beneficiary enterprises prepare Sustainability Plans and green investment proposals; monitor product uptake with scope to adjust instrument design/eligibility criteria, subject to Bank approval.
